source.title: Neglected crops: 1492 from a different perspective
source.role: Historical crop presence and colonial introduction; no population or yield fit

negative_domains.interpretation: FAO 1994 printed pp. 25 and 29 (PDF 46/50) identifies Iberian colonial introduction of wheat, barley, rye and rice. This extension covers Mexico and mainland Central America using pinned Natural Earth country geometry; it makes no Greenland/Norse or Canada/United States claim. Oryza keys are not Zizania. Original South American exclusions remain in the baseline.

records.source_locator: Printed p. 25 / PDF p. 46: indigenous maize farming in the established Mesoamerican agricultural tradition preceding introduced wheat
records.geographic_basis: Explicit named agricultural-system crosswalk to Anahuac in central Mesoamerica; no blanket maize availability assigned to northern Mexican hunter-gatherer areas. Crop presence is regional historical inference, not a dated individual field excavation.
records.interpretation: Maize was part of the pre-Columbian agricultural system. Availability only; no additional hectares, double harvest, attained-yield or population floor. The 1337 date denotes the modeled pre-contact state, not a precisely dated archaeological maize find.
